slides.texte_overlay:
7 social hacks for awkward moments
that feel like cheating
Waved back at someone who was actually waving at the person behind you? Just keep the wave going and grin. Owning it with a laugh is way less awkward than freezing in place.
Lost your train of thought mid-story? Say "Okay, I lost it. It was going to be amazing." Everyone laughs, someone helps you find it, and you look more relaxed than if you'd pushed through.
Both started talking at the same time? Say "No, go ahead" and mean it. Then actually ask about what they were saying. Letting someone go first costs nothing and makes them like you more.

When the silence drags, have something to bring up. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. "Random, but did you know honey basically never goes bad?" A weird fact saves almost any quiet moment.
slides.texte_sophia: When the silence drags, have something to bring up. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. A weird fact saves almost any quiet moment.

slides.texte_overlay: Didn't catch what someone said for the third time? Stop nodding. Say "Sorry, it's so loud in here, say that again?" Blame the room. Pretending you heard is how you end up agreeing to weird stuff.
Ran into someone you know but you're in a rush? Smile, slow down, and say "So good to see you, I'm running late, let's catch up soon." Warm and short always beats awkward and long.

Someone shares big news and you have nothing to add? Ask "So how does it feel?" Works for a new job, an engagement, a finished marathon. People love saying it out loud, and you needed no perfect line.
